TITLE: Edgard in Kimeria
NEW_GAME_CONFIRMATION: Start a new game? Your saved progress will be replaced.
MENU_HINT: Arrows/Tab to move - Enter/Space/A to confirm - Esc/B to go back
INTRO_LEAF_1:
Hear my tale of Kimeria, and hear it to the end.

Once upon a time, beyond the dark woods and the deep rivers, there lay the kingdom of Kimeria. King Rufardus the Wise ruled it, and it was fair beyond telling in a tale or writing with a pen.
INTRO_LEAF_2:
One day the witch L'Kardina came to that kingdom, for a neighbouring land had banished her.

But Kimeria would not keep her either. When the kingdom tried to drive her away, her fury turned into a terrible curse.
INTRO_LEAF_3:
From that hour the sun ceased to shine. Darkness swallowed the land, its fields, its woods and its towns.

And over the sleeping kingdom settled a night that had no end.
INTRO_LEAF_4:
Word of Kimeria's misfortune flew far and wide, and at last it reached Edgard, a wandering warrior: no king and no prince, only a man with a sword and a road under his feet.

He set out to overthrow the witch and save the kingdom.
INTRO_LEAF_5:
Whether his road was long or short, on it he met me, an old healer. I gave him my counsel and three gifts for the road:

a silver thread tied about his wrist, its other end kept in my hand; a spark of my own fire; and a fairy, one of the little lights the night could not put out.
INTRO_LEAF_6:
Ahead of him lay unfamiliar paths and cunning traps. A tale is soon told, but a deed is not soon done.

All this was only the saying. The tale is yet to come: Edgard's road through the sleeping kingdom begins here.
ENDING_STORY:
Hear how my tale ends. From that forest Edgard walked a long road, and I guided him as I had promised. He defeated every enemy, and not one monster was left in Kimeria.

Then the sun shone again, and the sleeping kingdom woke to the light. So ends my tale of Kimeria.

THE END

HEALER_GREETING: Edgard, beyond this glade the forest guardian keeps the road. An elixir from my pot would make your sword bite deep, but it will not touch my fire.
HEALER_RETURN_GREETING: So the road has brought you back, Edgard. Good.
HEALER_RETURN_CHECK: A bat wing, a mushroom and every coin of this forest: that is my price. Now show me what the forest has given you.
EDGARD_REPLY: Then brew it, old man. What does your pot ask for?
HEALER_INGREDIENTS: Every coin of this forest is with you, yet my pot stands hungry: the wood still hides a bat wing, a mushroom, or both.
HEALER_PAYMENT: The bat wing and the mushroom are here, but not my price. I take every coin of this forest; the coins of other lands are worth nothing to me.
HEALER_BOTH: My pot stands hungry and my price is not yet met. The elixir asks a bat wing, a mushroom and every coin of this forest.
HEALER_READY: All is gathered: the bat wing, the mushroom and every coin of this forest. Drink my elixir, and your sword will strike the guardian ten times harder.
HEALER_OFFER: I can send you back to where this forest begins, to seek what you missed. Or face the guardian without my elixir; once you meet him, no road leads back.
HEALER_PAID: Edgard, my price is paid and my elixir runs in your veins. Your sword strikes the guardian ten times harder now, but my fire burns no hotter.
HEALER_LOCK: Should the night swallow you, I will draw the silver thread, and my elixir will stay in you until the guardian falls. Go on.
HEALER_VICTORY: Edgard, the forest guardian has fallen, and the old wood breathes again. The road beyond lies open to you.
EDGARD_DARKNESS: Yet darkness still lies over all Kimeria, old man.
HEALER_GUIDE: Then your tale is not over, Edgard, and I will be your guide in it. Go on: we will meet again.
ABOUT_RULES: One hit kills; attempts are unlimited. Retry from this room; new pickups roll back, secured ones stay kept. Tap jump for each jump. Accessibility extends trap warnings.
ABOUT_GAME_STORY: A remake of a 1994 DOS game. Edgard, a wandering warrior, crosses the sleeping kingdom of Kimeria to break the witch L'Kardina's curse of eternal night.
ABOUT_GAME_PLAY: Swing the sword, throw fire, pull levers and read each trap before it springs. One hit ends an attempt, and every retry is instant.
ABOUT_GAME_MORE: Face the forest guardian with the help of an old healer. Play on keyboard, gamepad or touch, in five languages.
ABOUT_RULES_CARRY: Carry one object; the sword stays usable. A throw costs no fireball.
STICK_HINT: Stick: move and climb. Push it up to pick up or use, down to put down.
HINT_TUTORIAL_WALK: Walk right to find the way out
HINT_TUTORIAL_WALK_TOUCH: Drag the stick right to find the way out
HINT_LEVER_TORCH: Use the lever to start the platform or stop it
HINT_LEVER_EXIT: Platform moving or still, the way is open. Head for the exit
HINT_LEVER_BOTH: Use the lever to move the ladder and the platform
HINT_LADDER_LEVER: Use the lever to lower the ladder or raise it
HINT_LADDER_CLIMB: Climb the ladder when it is down
HINT_WALL_LEVER: Use the lever to raise the wall or lower it
HINT_WALL_PASS: Walk under the wall once it is raised
HINT_PLATFORM_LEVER: Use the lever to start the platform or stop it
HINT_PLATFORM_RIDE: Jump on the platform and ride it up to the exit
HINT_STONE_THROW: Carry the stone to the chasm and throw it at the lever
HINT_STONE_EXIT: Hit the lever with the stone, then ride the platform across
HINT_TRAP_PLATFORM: A cracked platform falls soon after you land. Cross quickly
HINT_TRAP_STUMP: A touched stump smokes, then explodes. Jump it or run clear
HINT_LADDER_ROOT: Thorns rise when you come near. Jump over them
HINT_WALL_BRANCH: A cracked branch falls just after you pass. Keep moving
HINT_PLATFORM_STONE: A shadow shows where a stone will fall. Step out of it
HINT_STONE_STUMP: This stump explodes when touched. Throw a stone or jump it
HEALER_TALE_ROAD: Listen, Edgard. The road ahead is short, yet it is a tale all the same, so hear it before you walk it.
EDGARD_TALE_NO_TIME: A tale? The kingdom waits, and I have no time for stories.
HEALER_TALE_FAIRIES: This wood is full of old handles. One wakes a sleeping torch, one lets down a ladder, and one moves a stubborn wall out of your way.
HEALER_TALE_LIFT: Another sets a boat of the air sailing up to the high ledge. What your hand cannot reach, a stone sent like a wish can wake.
HEALER_TALE_WITCH: Beware the wicked witch's gifts: thorns that rise, branches, stones and bridges that fall, and stumps that burst. Answer her riddles with quick feet.
HEALER_TALE_THREAD: Edgard, I tied a silver thread about your wrist, and I hold the other end. When the night swallows you, I draw the thread, and you will rise again at the path's edge.
HEALER_TALE_FIREGIFT: And one more gift, Edgard. Here is a spark of my own fire, and it will leap from your hand at what you fear. Sparks found on the road are this same fire, but it is not endless, so spend it as you would your last bread.
HEALER_TALE_FAIRY: And my last gift, Edgard: a fairy, one of the little lights the night could not put out. When you reach for a thing, she flies to it and lights it.
EDGARD_TALE_UNDERSTOOD: I understand, old man. Now let me go, the kingdom cannot wait.
HEALER_TALE_PRAISE: Well done, Edgard. The enchanted wood has told you all its tales, and you have solved every one of its riddles.
EDGARD_TALE_READY: Forgive my haste, healer. Am I ready for the road, then?
HEALER_TALE_HEROES: Ready as the heroes of old tales, who were afraid and went on all the same. A true warrior needs no more than that.
HEALER_TALE_BLESSING: Take my blessing: walk lightly, look keenly, and trust no path that seems too kind, for the witch smiles sweetest. May your fairy light your road. Go on.
HEALER_FIRST_DEATH: Edgard, the night swallowed you, so I drew the silver thread, and you rise again at the path's edge. Go on.
